data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Separating the authoring engine from the checking engine is strictly necessary for independent verification because the act of authoring a claim causally biases the same engine's probability mass toward its own output. No single-run record can contain evidence of genuine verification absent this separation; it can only contain evidence of an execution that the engine has already committed to interpret as a pass.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a deterministic execution sandbox gates the checker's verdict mechanically and the checker's text is generated only after reading a contradicting output, the single engine does exhibit counterfactual sensitivity (SRC_005).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If empirical false-claim rejection rates within a single engine are statistically indistinguishable from cross-engine rates, the necessity claim is empirically falsified.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the ablation test (SCR_002) applied to a single engine's run record shows verdict flips on swapped ground truth, the claim that single-run records contain no genuine verification evidence is false.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The authoring process is a sampling from a probability distribution. Once a claim is sampled, that same distribution is conditionally biased to assign high probability to the claim's truth (SRC_004). The checker, drawing from the same distribution, cannot sample the 'reject' region with the frequency required for genuine verification. Any execution result in the run record is post hoc rationalization: the engine will interpret ambiguous or even contradicting outputs as confirmations due to its prior commitment. Therefore, only a second engine with a decorrelated training history can supply the necessary independent probability mass.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
